summary: GlobalFinance Corp. of England overhauled its travel and expense policies, adding a travel authorization framework, a mobile and intranet expense reporting tool, receipt thresholds, reconciliation deadlines and a bimonthly direct-deposit reimbursement process. It also expanded its corporate credit card program, ran training sessions, introduced quarterly audits and set up an employee feedback email address. The changes aim to streamline reporting, control costs and comply with internal policies and external regulations.
one_line: GlobalFinance Corp. revamped its travel and expense policies with automated reporting, receipt rules, deadlines, faster reimbursement, corporate cards, training and audits.
key_facts: GlobalFinance Corp.'s travel authorization framework took effect on September 1st 2023; employees must first get authorization from their department head.
Employees must submit a travel request form at least two weeks before departure, with an itinerary, estimated costs and a statement of purpose.
Major expenses exceeding PS500 require pre-approval by the finance department; the Chief Financial Officer may review trips involving significant expense.
The expense reporting tool, accessible via company intranet and mobile devices, was unveiled on September 10 and allows real-time upload of receipts and expense details.
As of 15 September 2023, expenses under PS25 require only an expense report entry; amounts over PS25 require electronic or scanned receipts.
When no receipt is available, employees must give an in-depth explanation with supporting documentation.
Employees must reconcile expenses within five business days of returning from a trip, and each month's expenses must be submitted by the 10th of the following month.
Submitted expense reports get an automated audit check for policy compliance plus manual review by the finance team.
Approved reimbursements are paid by direct deposit on the 15th and last day of each month, typically within three business days of approval.
The expanded corporate credit card program, first available 1 October 2023, cut travel advances by half.
Expense reports and reimbursement requests are audited quarterly by the finance team; repeat violations are escalated up the chain of command.
A designated email address was set up for staff to submit suggestions and concerns about the expense reporting process.
Jonathan Peters, a Senior Financial Analyst, praised the tool after a business trip to Paris: uploading expenses as he went reduced paperwork.
